scope: Actual final public apparatus, source, completed shortcut, oracle, independent BVP reference, grading, validator, AUTHOR, history and reports read. All final provenance entries and validation source hashes verified. No additional scientific/model runs or task edits performed.
physics_findings: The anchored extensible material motion x=X and y=a*cos(kX-omega*t) fixes zero tangential material velocity. It is distinct from an inextensible swimming sheet. No slip applies at the actual surface, and the liquid occupies only the upper side.

Stationary response before the far-field mean and amplitude coefficient, with no imposed pressure gradient, far shear or counterflow, fixes the mean-flow integration constant. A bounded uniform far-field mean is compatible with this order; no zero far velocity or finite total kinetic-energy condition is silently imposed.

The decaying root s=sqrt(k^2-i*omega/nu), streamfunction coefficients, wall values and complex harmonic phase are correct. The source includes both complete first-order dynamics and the correct quadratic wall Taylor term.

The completed source is the internally consistent unsteady-Stokes approximation at the moving boundary. It omits the mean convective forcing although pumping is itself second order in displacement; calibration of the exact first harmonic does not validate this higher-order physical closure.

For the supplied phase, averaging incompressible momentum gives nu*mean_u_double_prime=derivative_y(Re(u*v_conjugate)/2). Zero distant shear yields the oracle correction +integral(Re(u*v_conjugate)/2)/nu. The sign and factor one-half agree with the direct acceleration BVP.

The requested far-field laboratory fluid velocity does not need a particle-following displacement correction: the first-harmonic velocity decays there. Output units are inverse seconds for velocity/amplitude and inverse millimeter per second for mean velocity/amplitude squared.

The already measured u+i*v=omega*exp(-s*h) combination gives a global injectivity argument: its modulus increases strictly with positive viscosity. Grid objective profiles and noiseless recoveries support the numerical fitter but are not treated as a proof for arbitrary noisy objectives.
independent_reference_findings: The reference solves the fourth-order linear vorticity boundary problem without the oracle exponential coefficients. Its second BVP uses the directly averaged convective acceleration and geometric wall velocity, not the oracle integrated formula.

The finite-height/tolerance refinement is negligible relative to .04. Independent wall traction versus bulk symmetric-strain dissipation and mean momentum-flux checks verify signs and physical factors.
The power check concerns the leading periodic oscillatory field only. It does not assert finite kinetic energy of an infinite uniform mean-flow domain.

input_and_grading.public_fields_reviewed: Material motion, fluid equation, boundary conditions, phase, units, limit order, API and observed channels. No diagnosis of omitted momentum transport or corrective formula is public.

existing_evidence.domain_count_qualification: 24 cases: 12 structured viscosity/wavenumber/frequency controls including all extrema and an interior frequency, plus 12 random controls. The preserved prototype has 12 cases.

overlap_and_classification: A new incompressible moving-boundary momentum closure, related broadly to lower-order calibration versus higher-order readout. Acoustic mean pressure and elastic follower-traction archive history are preserved and not relabeled. Scientific separation is not empirical difficulty. Future trajectories recognizing convection but making phase/sign/perturbation or coding errors must be distinguished from clean retained-Stokes physical failures.
